name: Isolated Radial Hemimelia

criteria.description: Congenital absence or hypoplasia of the radius bone
Hypoplasia or aplasia of the thumb on the affected limb
Ulnar deviation of the hand due to radial deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital absence or hypoplasia of the radius with associated thumb hypoplasia or aplasia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiographic; genetic testing may be used to exclude syndromic associations.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Deviation of the hand or of fingers of the hand

imaging: X-ray showing absent or hypoplastic radius
Radiographic evidence of thumb hypoplasia or aplasia
Ultrasound or MRI to assess soft tissue and associated anomalies
other: Clinical examination revealing radial deviation and limb shortening

distinguishingFeatures: Family history of autosomal dominant inheritance
Multiple congenital anomalies beyond radial deficiency

redFlags: Presence of cardiac abnormalities requiring urgent evaluation
Signs of bone marrow failure or hematological abnormalities
Progressive neurological deficits or nerve compression symptoms
references: Biesecker LG. The limb malformation syndromes. Pediatr Clin North Am. 2010;57(3):591-607.
Goldfarb CA, Manske PR. Radial longitudinal deficiency: current concepts. J Am Acad Orthop Surg. 2009;17(3):163-171.
